subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Currency Crisis Contagion
description: A short lesson to help you apply Currency Crisis Contagion.

hook.text: Thailand's baht collapses in 1997. Within months, currencies crash across Malaysia, Indonesia, and South Korea.

buildup.text: Currency crises spread through contagion — investors flee all similar markets when one falls, creating a domino effect.

discovery.text: The 1997 Asian financial crisis wiped out decades of economic gains across Southeast Asia in a single year.

twist.text: Indonesia's crisis toppled President Suharto after 31 years. Currency crises become political crises.

climax.text: Contagion means that one country's currency problem quickly becomes a regional or global economic emergency.

punchline.text: One currency falls. Investors flee. The region collapses.

quiz.question: What is currency crisis contagion?
options: When one country's currency collapse spreads to others in the region
When all currencies gain value simultaneously
A deliberate government policy to devalue currency
